title: Eval smoke-suite and confidence thresholds for canary auto-recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Current canary rollouts rely on multi-metric dashboards and post-hoc human review to detect quality regressions on eval prompt sets. This is slow and error-prone for small but impactful quality drops that require immediate rollback or controlled mitigation. Goal: implement a lightweight 'eval smoke-suite' that runs a compact per-customer and global prompt set during canary and shadow traffic, combined with model output confidence thresholds and a short-circuit auto-recovery path. The feature must support: (1) stable, reproducible per-canary score calculation, (2) configurable confidence bands per prompt and per-customer, (3) deterministic trigger rules for auto-heal, rollback, or traffic diversion, (4) observability hooks and audit trail for decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Smoke-suite runs automatically for every canary flip and for shadowed model variants; 2) Score delta calculation is stable across identical inputs and recorded in the rollout trace; 3) Confidence thresholds configurable via Console and per-release config; 4) When thresholds are breached, the orchestrator performs one of: auto-divert to baseline model, scale down variant, or full rollback, according to policy; 5) All decisions produce audit events with prompt set ids, score diffs, and user-visible reason in the rollout UI; 6) Unit/integration tests cover gating logic, threshold tuning UI, and fallback action; 7) Latency regression remains within SLOs for smoke-suite (<=50ms p50 extra for canary path), and cost increase limited to 2% for typical canaries.
implementation_notes:
Design:
- Create a minimal smoke-suite runner service that accepts a canary id, model variant id, and prompt-set id, then computes a fixed set of metrics (fidelity score, hallucination indicator, token-level confidence aggregate, safety flag). The runner must be deterministic for identical seed and model weights.
- Add per-prompt 'confidence band' metadata: baseline_score, tolerated_delta, min_confidence. Store bands in configstore and expose through Console.
- Integrate runner into the rollout orchestrator: pre-flip check, continuous shadow checks, and post-flip verification. Runner outputs metric bundle -> gating engine.
- Gating engine evaluates a small DSL: if weighted_delta > threshold OR any prompt min_confidence < min_confidence_limit then trigger action.
- Actions: AUTO_DIVERT (route traffic back to baseline via smart-routing), SCALE_DOWN (reduce canary weight by 50% and run next check), ROLLBACK (full revert). Actions are annotated and emitted as audit events.
- Provide an offline scoring tool to re-run smoke-suite against historical traces for threshold tuning.
- Implement feature flags to roll out to internal orgs first.
Tradeoffs:
- Running smoke-suite synchronously adds cost/latency; prefer shadow-run where possible. For strict pre-flip checks, run small prompt subset.
- Confidence signals vary by model family; we need per-model calibration. Initial rollout uses conservative thresholds to avoid false positives.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal): enable smoke-suite for internal orgs only, default policy = NO_AUTO_ACTION (alerts only). Duration: 2 weeks. Phase 2 (Beta): enable AUTO_DIVERT for non-critical customers, threshold conservative (-1.5% weighted score). Duration: 4 weeks. Phase 3 (GA): expose policy controls in Console (AUTO_DIVERT/SCALE_DOWN/ROLLBACK) and allow per-customer override. Gradually expand to 100% of canaries.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: smoke_suite.run_count, smoke_suite.latency_ms, smoke_suite.weighted_delta, smoke_suite.prompt_min_confidence_percentile, canary.gate_triggered_count. Alerts: Pager when gate triggers for enterprise customers (>=1 trigger within rolling 15m) and severity high. Create dashboard tile in Console showing rolling 24h heatmap by prompt set and model family. All gate events should include links to related rollout traces, smoke-suite raw outputs, and PR/Design doc.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive auto-actions could cause unnecessary rollbacks impacting availability. Mitigation: Conservative thresholds, internal-only trial, and gradual beta. Risk: Confidence metric calibration drift across quantized and non-quantized variants. Mitigation: Per-model calibration job and a fallback to syntactic heuristics. Risk: Storage bloat from recording smoke-suite outputs. Mitigation: TTL policy and sampling for non-enterprise orgs.
